title: The centre column of Rule 30 is never periodic
credit: S. Wolfram, Rule 30 Prize Problem 1 (2019); partial result E. Jen (1986/1990).
premise_risks: An unrefereed 2022 arXiv preprint (2207.13237) claims a solution; it has not been accepted
Well known, so novelty is low
plain: Rule 30 is the one-dimensional cellular automaton in which each cell's new colour is (left) XOR (centre OR right). Start from a single black cell on an infinite white row and record the colour of the starting cell at each time step. Prove that this 0/1 sequence is not eventually periodic.
math: Let $x_0:\mathbb{Z}\to\{0,1\}$ with $x_0(0)=1$ and $x_0(j)=0$ for $j\ne0$, and $x_{t+1}(j)=x_t(j-1)\oplus\big(x_t(j)\vee x_t(j+1)\big)$. Let $c_t=x_t(0)$. Prove that there are no $p\ge1$ and $T\ge0$ with $c_{t+p}=c_t$ for all $t\ge T$.
